clue.text: Not, it may be said, a leg of mutton

explanation.surface: A pedantic remark that something is not, apparently, a leg of mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not, it may be said' is KNOT spoken aloud, and a sheepshank is a knot for shortening rope; read literally, the word is a sheep's shank, a leg of mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a sailor's knot (the word 'Not' sounded out); the second takes the word apart as a sheep's lower leg, which is meat called mutton.

clue.text: Thus the sovereign is below par

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
K is king, a sovereign

explanation.surface: The monarch is feeling a little unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling unwell is being below par, under one's normal health.

clue.text: Garden emptied by autumn in the States?

definitions.text: Garden emptied by autumn in the States?

parts.words: Garden emptied by autumn in the States?
parts.note: Americans call autumn the Fall, and the biblical Fall of Man got Adam and Eve thrown out of their garden

explanation.surface: An American garden left bare when autumn comes.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise garden was emptied when Adam and Eve were expelled after the Fall.

clue.text: Penchant of model prince to idle

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model's prince who likes doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking or fondness for something is a penchant.

clue.text: Was reluctant to make death-mask

indicators.note: to mask is to disguise, so the word before it appears in disguise, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who did not want to make a death-mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link; 'death-mask' splits into the fodder and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongly disliked, as a loose sense of being reluctant or loath to do something.

clue.text: You must find domestic help after sister gets married

indicators.note: after puts the help behind the sister and the married letter

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital
aid means help

explanation.surface: Once her sister marries, you will have to find other household help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic help' reads as one phrase, but 'domestic' alone is the definition and 'help' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children is a household servant, a domestic.

clue.text: Stone is a little too pale

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gemstone described as only slightly too pale in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This iridescent gem is a precious stone.

clue.text: Does this stop drivers being over the limit?

definitions.text: Does this stop drivers being over the limit?

parts.words: Does this stop drivers being over the limit?
parts.note: over the limit suggests drink-driving, but here it means exceeding the speed limit, which a concealed police check catches

explanation.surface: A question about stopping drunk drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed speed check by officers catches motorists exceeding the speed limit.

clue.text: Their advances attract a great deal of interest

definitions.text: Their advances attract a great deal of interest

parts.words: Their advances attract a great deal of interest
parts.note: advances are loans and interest is the charge on them, not romantic attention

explanation.surface: Someone whose romantic advances draw plenty of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortionate moneylenders make loans that carry very high interest.

clue.text: It sounds as if transparent lie is seen through in church

indicators.note: the clue says outright that what follows is matched by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a transparent lie is a clear story, a falsehood anyone can see through

explanation.surface: An obvious falsehood is exposed during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen through' sounds like the lie being exposed, but the definition means the upper row of windows in a church, which light passes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's upper storey of windows above the aisle roofs is something you look through.

clue.text: Prayer sure to leave feeling of satisfaction

indicators.note: sure is told to go away, so those letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: pleasure is a feeling of satisfaction

explanation.surface: Someone sure they will leave a prayer feeling satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest request or entreaty is a kind of prayer.

clue.text: A meeting of the ways in remote place in Somerset?

explanation.surface: Roads meeting somewhere remote in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in Somerset, a county in south-west England, so a remote spot in Street is a corner of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two roads meet is a junction; the second reading is a corner, an out-of-the-way spot, in the Somerset town of Street.

clue.text: Falsifies marks? Rubbish

parts.note: to fiddle accounts is to falsify them
ticks are marks on a page

explanation.surface: A teacher accused of faking grades dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation meaning nonsense, used to dismiss something as rubbish.

clue.text: Having nothing to learn, income isn't bad

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone who knows everything and says their income is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: All-knowing, so there is nothing left to learn.

clue.text: Grave undertakings?

parts.note: grave looks like serious, and undertakings like enterprises, but read as the work of undertakers putting people in graves

explanation.surface: Serious enterprises.
explanation.definitionFit: Burials are the business of undertakers, placing bodies in graves.

clue.text: Amen to sin represented the state of St Paul

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order, so this word signals the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A religious phrase about sin stands for the state whose capital is named after an apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul here is the capital city of a US state, not the apostle the 'Amen to sin' surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midwestern US state whose capital city is St Paul.

clue.text: Old bird is for ages wrongly identified with osprey

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An ancient bird that has for years been mistaken for an osprey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identified with osprey' adds that the old name was applied to the osprey as well as the lammergeier.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic name for the lammergeier, also applied to the osprey: an old name for a bird.

clue.text: One of the film crowd -he's super

explanation.surface: A background actor in a crowd scene boasts that he is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'super' is short for supernumerary, the theatre word for a walk-on performer, and also means additional; 'he's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A film background performer is so called; super means supernumerary, an additional person beyond the regular cast.

clue.text: Still slow

explanation.definitionFit: Motionless matter is still, and a sluggish person is slow to act.

clue.text: Deflect from party lines

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game
a railway track is a pair of lines

explanation.surface: To steer someone away from following the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone from their main purpose is to deflect them.

clue.text: For this and 15. 5 is the usual consideration

parts.note: common means usual or ordinary
a factor is a consideration that affects a decision

explanation.surface: A remark about the usual considerations for this clue and another.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'this' as the answer itself and '15' and '5' as numbers: 5 divides both 15 and 5, so it is what they share.
explanation.definitionFit: A number dividing two others exactly is what they share; 5 divides 15 and itself.

clue.text: University match could be a stunner

parts.note: CU stands for Cambridge University
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A varsity sports fixture could be a cracking game.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person is a cutie, a stunner.

clue.text: Temptation is torment!

explanation.surface: Declaring that being tempted is a torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is a temptation; to bait someone is to torment or tease them.

clue.text: Mind what you pay!

explanation.surface: A warning to watch what you spend.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice is to mind; attention is what one pays when told to pay attention.

clue.text: 'E's talking about Navy flier

indicators.note: about means round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: read as Es, the plural of the letter E: two Es
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A Cockney sailor holding forth about the Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes "'E's" look like Cockney for 'he's'; read it as two letter Es that go around RN. 'talking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea eagle is a bird, and so a flier.

clue.text: Reverse vehicle in high wind? What a gamble!

indicators.note: reverse tells you to turn the word for a vehicle backwards

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle
a gale is a high wind

explanation.surface: Backing a car up in a strong gale is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting system of doubling the stake after each loss is a notorious gamble.

clue.text: One of Cowper's works

parts.note: William Cowper, the 18th-century English poet, wrote a long blank-verse poem with this title, which is also a word for a piece of work

explanation.surface: A reference to a poem by William Cowper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's best-known long poem bears this title, and the word also means a job of work.

clue.text: Went in, being bored

explanation.surface: Someone entered a place while feeling bored.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or enter something is to go in; a drilled hole means the material was bored through.
